messages.subject: geno.table column names
parts:
Hi, 

I run the geno.table function and these are the column names of the output 

>myCross=read.cross("csvr",".","myInputFile.csvr",skip=1,genotypes=NULL,crosstype="4way")
> myOutput=geno.table(myCross,scanone.output=TRUE)
> colnames(myOutput)
 [1] "chr"       "pos"       "neglog10P" "missing"   "ANA"       "BNA"       "ANA.1"     "BNA.1"     "A"        
[10] "B"         "N"         "N.1"       "ANA.BNA"   "BNA.ANA"   "not.ANA"   "not.BNA"   "not.ANA.1" "not.BNA.1"

What does ANA , BNA ANA.1 and BNA.1 fields means ??  All the other fields (A, B, N , N.1 etc. are zero in my case)

I know these are supposed to be the count of genotypes in that location my cross is a four way cross ab x cd so I am expecting to see 4 possible genotypes in the progeny ac ad bc bd 

I am confused of the "NA" is that a missing genotypes ? It should not be because my input is phased and there are no missing genotypes.

I will appreciate if you can clarify this.

Thanks a lot
Best Regards
Hamdi

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: geno.table column names
parts:
I'm not absolutely certain, but it seems like the cross object, myCross, ended up with allele labels c("A", "B"), and it needs four allele labels.
Maybe we you read the data with read.cross(), you included alleles=c("A", "B")?

Try modifying the allele attribute for the cross:

  attr(myCross, "alleles") <- LETTERS[1:4]

karl

parts:
Dear Karl,
Thanks for your reply. This fixes the issue. I did not set the alleles=c("A","B") parameter but it seems although this is a "4way" cross the default parameter is set as c("A","B"). I also tried to set this as alleles=c("A","B","C","D") but this does not work either. I need to read the cross and then fix the attribute alleles as you suggested. There is also another problem with 4way crosses (I posted this on a another thread) basically now when I read a 4way cross I use the following function to fix the object. I just wanted to share this since it might be helpful to others as well.  

fix_4way_Cross_Object <- function(myCross) #This fix is needed for any cross objects created with crosstype="4way"
{
  
  for(i in 1:length(myCross$geno))
  {
    a=as.matrix(myCross$geno[[i]]$map)
    myCross$geno[[i]]$map=t(cbind(a,a[,1]))
  }
  attr(myCross, "alleles") <- LETTERS[1:4]  #change the allele attribute to include 4 alleles A B C D
  
  return(myCross)
  
}


control=read.cross("csvr",".","control.csvr",skip=1,genotypes=NULL,crosstype="4way")
control=fix_4way_Cross_Object(control)

Thanks
Best Regards
Hamdi
